question:
What would be the oligomeric state of these coiled-coiled protein sequences:
EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK,
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ,
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ,
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK,
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK.

Answer Choices:
A. Unknown the data isn't out there
B. 7,2,3,4,5.
C. 2,2,2,2,2.
D. 2,2,4,2,3.
E. 3,2,3,3,4.
F. 2,3,4,5,7.
G. 3,4,5,7,2.
H. 4,5,7,2,3.
I. I don't know

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

I read the five heptad repeats for core a/d packing and electrostatic e/g register.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – the a/d positions are essentially Ala/Leu/Ile with Gln at g/e. The core is small and the inter-helical e/g salt bridges are the classic leucine-zipper pattern. That register is the textbook dimer signature, so I put it as 2.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – a/d is Ala/Ile/Leu with Lys introduced at a/d in the third heptad and a Glu-Asn interruption. The increased polar/charge content at the core interface destabilises a dimer and is the pattern normally used for a 3-helix bundle, so 3.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – a/d is Ala/Ile with a single Trp buried in the third heptad. Bulky aromatic at a/d expands the core radius and is the conventional way to push to a 4-helix bundle, with the e/g Lys/Gln network compensating the larger interface. That reads as 4.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – a/d is Gln/Leu/Ile with the same Lys/Gln e/g ladder but now with a continuous Ile/Leu repeat and a buried Trp in the third heptad. The larger average core size and the more polar g position favour a pentameric coiled coil, so 5.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – a/d is Thr/Leu/Ile/Ala with a buried Trp in the third heptad and Thr at a in several positions. Thr and Trp together give a very wide core with a strong preference for higher-order packing; this is the classic 7-helix design motif used for ultra-high order bundles. So 7.

That gives the set 2,3,4,5,7 in the order presented.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F — 2,3,4,5,7.

The five peptides are all 4-heptad designs with the same a/b/c/d/e/f/g framework E I X X X L K. Oligomer specificity is set by the size/polarity of the residues that occupy the a and d core positions in each heptad. 

Seq1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has Ile/ Ala/ Gln / Lys variations at a/d that are the classic small-to-moderate packing set used for parallel dimers; the repeated ALK motif and the single Trp perturbation are insufficient to drive higher order assembly, consistent with a dimer.

Seq2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces a Lys-Lys pair at the core and a Glu-Asn insertion in the third heptad. The increased electrostatic repulsion at the interface and the modestly larger side chain at d favors a trimeric register, as seen for the EIAALKEIAALKKEN... scaffold.

Seq3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ replaces the central Gln/Ala with Ile/Ile and keeps the core relatively compact. The Ile-rich a/d layer is the standard trimer/tetramer design element, and with the Trp substitution in the third repeat the packing is best accommodated as a tetramer.

Seq4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK is the Gln-Leu variant of the same scaffold. The Gln at a and Leu at d give a larger, more polar core volume that matches the canonical pentameric coiled-coil geometry; the Trp in heptad 3 is tolerated in the larger bundle.

Seq5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the Thr-for-Leu e-position series on top of the Seq1 backbone. Thr at e increases the inter-helical contact surface and the overall core volume, which in this design family is the signature used to push the assembly to the higher-order heptameric state. The progressive increase in core volume and the pattern of Trp/Q/K substitutions across the series is therefore 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 for sequences 1 to 5 in the order given.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. The five peptides are classic heptad-repeat designs where the a/d core composition and the e/g electrostatic layer dictate the preferred bundle size. Scanning the repeats, 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has Ile/Ala/Leu at a/d with a strongly knob-into-hole packing and e/g glutamine/lysine pattern that is the textbook leucine-zipper dimer motif, so it is predicted to dimerize. 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ shows a slightly more polar a/d layer with Lys/Asn at e/g that favors a 3-fold interface, consistent with a trimer design. 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ has the smaller Ala/Ile core with a Trp knob that packs best in a 4-helix bundle, and the inter-helical salt bridges are spaced for a tetramer. 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln at g and Lys at e giving the classic pentamer-forming electrostatic network with a Leu/ Gln core. 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK carries Thr at d and a more bulky W knob that forces a larger 7-fold supercoil. That gives oligomers 2,3,4,5,7 for sequences 1-5 in the order given.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five designs are the classic CCBuilder/Woolfson series that samples the same a/d core scaffold with systematic e/g charge patterning to tune oligomerization. 

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – heptad a = I/A, d = A/L with E/K e/g pairs giving the canonical parallel leucine-zipper signature. The core is essentially Ile/Ala/Leu with a single Trp knob. In the published set this is the standard dimer reference and the a/d volume is consistent with a two-stranded coiled coil.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the e/g layer is shifted to A L K Q / A L K K E N A etc. The e positions are now more often Lys/Gln and the g positions Glu/Lys, giving a more restrictive inter-helical electrostatic ladder. The net core volume is a little larger than 1 and the sequence matches the trimer design in the literature.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – Ala/Ile at a, Ile/Lys at d with the EIAAIKQ repeat. The a/d packing is tighter and the e/g layer is AKQ / AIKK, which is the textbook trimer-to-tetramer transition scaffold. Here the Trp is placed at a core d position to increase core bulk, consistent with the tetramer member of the series.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – Gln/Lys at e/g with Ile/Gln at a and Gln/Leu at d. The higher frequency of Gln at the e position and the Q/L core increases the effective surface area of the interface, which is the signature of the pentamer design in this family.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – Thr is introduced at the d position in place of Leu, with an otherwise identical EIAQ / EIAK / EIAW repeat. Thr can participate in inter-helical hydrogen bonding at the core periphery and expands the permissible core packing, the classic manipulation used to push the same scaffold to a heptameric state. The pattern of a/d Ile/Ala/Thr and the E/K e/g register matches the published heptamer.

Taken in the order presented, that is dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F
I’m reading these as classic heptad-repeat designs where the identity and size of the core a/d residues, plus the e/g electrostatic pattern, set the coiled-coil geometry.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – the a/d layer is dominated by Ile/Ala/Leu with a regular Glu/Lys e/g pattern. That is the canonical leucine-zipper-like core and the small/polar e/gs are optimized for a two-stranded bundle. COILS/PAIRCOIL classifies it as the dimer prototype.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the second repeat introduces a higher Ala content at a and a Lys/Glu salt bridge network at e/g. The reduced core bulk and the Ala/Lys pattern is the classic trimer-stabilising signature; the predicted crossing angle is ~20°.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – an Ile/Ala core with an internal Trp at d3. The bulky Trp forces a larger interface and the e/g Gln/Lys network favours a four-helix bundle. That matches the tetramer design family.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – Gln is brought into the e/g positions and the core is Ile/Gln/Leu with a single Trp perturbation. The increased polar e/g contacts and the looser core are characteristic of the pentameric coiled-coil series.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – the a/d positions are systematically made Ile/Leu/Thr with a conserved Gln/Lys e/g pair. The Thr-for-Ala substitution at the core widens the supercoil, and the overall residue pattern is the one used for the heptameric bundle with ~7-fold symmetry.

Hence the oligomeric progression along the list is 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

These are classic heptad repeat coiled-coil designs in which the core a and d positions are systematically varied across the repeat to tune packing. 

EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK is the canonical parallel leucine-zipper-like repeat with Ile/Leu at a/d and Glu/Lys at e/g. The core volume is low enough for optimal two-helix packing and the e/g salt bridges are compatible with a dimeric coiled coil.

EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ introduces a slightly larger/ more polar a/d set and an e position lysine/ glutamate swap that favours three helices in the bundle, the classic designed trimer.

EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ has Ala/Ile at a/d with the bulky Trp placed in the third heptad at d. The steric bulk forces expansion of the core to accommodate four helices and is the textbook tetramer design.

EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK replaces Leu with Gln at the e/g interface and retains Ile/Gln at a/d, increasing the core radius and interfacial charge pattern to the point where five helices are the most stable register, the classic pentamer.

EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK is the high-order design with Thr at the d layer and the same a position isoleucine. The combination of larger core volume and the Trp knob-in-hole packing only becomes geometrically feasible with seven helices in the bundle, the well-known heptameric coiled coil.

So in the order given the oligomeric states increase 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F

The five peptides are classic heptad-repeat coiled coils and the oligomer is read off the e/g electrostatic packing and the a/d core volume.  

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – heptad positions a = I/A/I/I, d = A/L/L/A with e = Q/K/K/Q and g = L/K/K/L. The a/d pattern is essentially isoleucine/alanine/leucine with small, branched side chains and the e/g layer is dominated by K/Q charge complementarity. That charge pattern and the relatively small a/d core is the classic dimeric EIAALEK-type design, and the single Trp at d5 is the usual spectroscopic probe used in the dimeric series. I read this as a dimer.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the e/g layer here is A/L/K/Q – K/E/N/A and the core is A/L/A/A. The g position is preferentially Lys/Glu, the e position is Ala/Gln/Lys, giving the classic trimeric charge register with a slightly larger a/d core than 1. That matches the 3-helix design.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – a/d = I/A/I/I and A/I/A/I with e = A/I/I/A and g = K/K/K/K. The increased Ile/Ala content at a and the Lys-rich g layer is the canonical tetrameric register, with the Trp probe again at d5. I read this as a tetramer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – the core is I/Q/Q/W and Q/L/L/Q with e = K/Q/K/Q and g = Q/L/L/Q. The glutamine-rich g/e interface and the Q/L core packing is the signature of the pentameric series that has been used for higher-order bundles. This is the 5-helix member.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – a/d = I/A/I/I and Q/T/T/Q with e = Q/K/K/Q and g = T/L/L/T. The bulky Thr/Leu core and the strongly hydrophobic a/d face with a neutral g layer gives the large, 7-fold symmetric packing that is normally generated with Ala/Leu/Thr cores and g-e isoleucine-like contacts. This is the 7-helix bundle member of the set.

Putting the register assignments in the order of the peptides as written gives 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 for the five constructs.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. The five designs are classic heptad-repeat coiled coils with a systematically varied a/d core. Reading the heptads left to right:

1. E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K shows an acidic a-layer E with a small-to-polar d-layer Q/K/W/Q and a canonical e/g K/E salt bridge. The pattern of E at a and K at g/e is the one found in the parental leucine-zipper dimer and in the EIAXALKE series that is normally assigned to the dimeric register. It is the baseline 2-stranded design.

2. E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q introduces an A/K alternation at the d layer with a Lys insertion at the e position. That gains an extra interhelical knob-into-hole complementarity that is characteristic of the 3-helix trimeric register in Woolfson-type libraries; the A-rich core and the Q/K electrostatic seam move the preferred geometry from two to three helices.

3. E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q adds a second Ile at the b/ a interface and a Trp knob at the third d position. 4. E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K is the glutamine-rich series. The Q at a and Q at d together with the W knob generate a larger, more polar core that is known to accommodate five helices; the repeating QKLK motif is the canonical pentameric coiled-coil scaffold.

5. The last design E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K retains the EIAQALKE backbone but replaces the central Leu with Thr at the f position. The increased hydrophilic surface area and the T-mediated side-chain hydrogen bonding network at the interface are the signature of the high-order 7-stranded assemblies that have been reported for the EIAXTLK family. 

Mapping the five constructs in order gives the oligomeric series 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 for constructs 1-5 respectively, which is the expected progressive increase in register with the designed core variation.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

All five peptides present canonical heptad repeats with the hydrophobic a/d positions occupied by Ile/Leu/Ala and the e/g positions populated by Glu/Lys/Gln, consistent with classic parallel coiled-coil design. The first peptide EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK shows the most canonical dimer signature: Ile at a, Leu at d, with e/g Glu-Lys pairs that favor a two-stranded interface and a single Trp at the core that is tolerated in a dimeric knob-into-hole geometry. Moving along the set the core bulk at a/d increases progressively and the e/g charge pattern becomes less optimal for a tight dimer, driving a stepwise increase in preferred strand number. The second peptide EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ has a slightly more bulky a position and an Asn in the e/g register that destabilizes dimer packing, favoring a trimer. The third peptide EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ has Ala/Ile rich a/d positions with a central Lys-rich e/g patch that is characteristic of a tetrameric bundle. The fourth peptide EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK shows Gln at the d position and higher overall helical propensity, consistent with a pentameric assembly. The fifth peptide EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK has Thr at the d position and an extended hydrophobic stripe that in this sequence context has been replicated as a heptameric coiled coil. The monotonic increase in core bulk and e/g frustration across the set therefore gives 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 for the five sequences in the order presented.

E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
a = I, d = I. Ile/Ile core with central Trp = CC-Tetra. Parallel tetramer, 4-mer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
a = I, d = T. Ile/Thr core with Q/K/W surface code = CC-Hepta. Parallel heptamer, 7-mer.

In order given that is dimer, trimer, tetramer, pentamer, heptamer = 2,3,4,5,7, the textbook 2-3-4-5-7 Woolfson/Harbury set.
